title: GPU SKU fallback attention orchestrator for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Jasmine Patel
description: Introduce an orchestrator that picks attention execution paths and graceful fallbacks based on GPU SKU, MIG partitioning, and current clock/thermal state to improve prefill + decode tail latency and reduce expensive kernel mismatches. This ticket implements heuristics, a lightweight scoring function, and a runtime-configurable policy to shift between fast-path attention kernels, tiled fallback kernels, or mixed-precision variants depending on topology and active clocks.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator integrates with the runtime kernel selector and exposes a policy flag (sku_fallback_policy)
Measured 95th percentile prefill latency improvement >= 8% for mixed-SKU clusters (H100 + A10) on representative workloads
No regression in functional correctness (all model inference outputs match baseline within numerical tolerance)
Automated integration test covering MIG split on L40S that simulates a clock-throttled path and validates fallback occurs within 2ms
Docs and console toggle added: README, runtime flag, and rollout playbook in Confluence
technical_decisions: Use a lightweight, deterministic scoring function (score = kernel_pref * avail_bw_weight * clock_headroom) rather than ML model to ensure explainability and reproducibility
Prioritize low-overhead heuristics in hot path; avoid dynamic compilation in selection step to keep decision latency <0.5ms
Fallback ordering: fast fused attention -> tiled int8 attention -> banked KV-streaming path -> CPU fallback, chosen to balance latency & GPU utilization
Clock steering interactions: prefer kernels that are more tolerant to reduced SM clocks when GPU clock_headroom < 10%
MIG-awareness: prefer kernels that avoid cross-slice NVLink transfers for fragmented MIG topologies to reduce inter-slice contention

testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring function corner cases (zero bandwidth, zero clock headroom)
Integration tests: simulated MIG topologies (1/2/4 slices) with mocked clock drops to validate fallback path triggers
A/B perf experiments on a small fleet (10% traffic) comparing default selector vs orchestrator
Stress test with mixed length batches to verify no OOM on A10 and no SV fault on L40S
Nightly regression run against numeric tolerance suite for key open models
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy orchestrator as opt-in flag for 10% of dedicated cluster capacity
Observe telemetry for selected_kernel distribution, error rates, and 95th percentile latency for 48h
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over two weeks if metrics stable
Automatic rollback if 95th percentile latency regresses by >5% or error rate increases >0.5%
Postmortem after full rollout to capture corner cases and update heuristics
